entries.title: encoder conformance gap — GlobalSemanticProfileV1 nominal contract (trunc-toward-zero division, checked overflow) vs the coincidence domains the encoder actually verifies
entries.description: SemanticProfileV1 nominally declares divisionMode=spDivTruncTowardZero and overflowMode=spOverflowBounded (src/core/trusted/semantic_profile.nim:100-101), but the encoder verifies Lean floor '/' and Int.emod '%' coinciding with Nim div/mod ONLY on the nonnegative domain (div/rem identity segments, src/verification/obligation/canonical_verification.nim:117,123; proofs/IR/Denotation.lean Certified forms), and does not model checked-overflow reachability — obligations discharge overflow instead (no-overflow obligations). The modelprofile identity segment landed 2026-10-07 (modelprofile=<SemanticProfileV1Hash>/no-overflow-obligations/coincident-checked-wrap-domain, identity.nim:118-131) therefore states the coincidence DOMAIN, not the full nominal mode; the certificate semanticProfileId continues to carry the nominal-profile hash (src/verification/cert_writer.nim:406-407), so a reader comparing the two sees a semantics gap that is real and untracked. Registered per authority_contract.md §5.3 (no unauthorized value generation — fail-closed) and base36_sizing_binding_contract.md §4.1; deliberately NOT patched in code by the binding PR (originally numbered DEBT#491 in the identity-binding PR; renumbered DEBT#494 after concurrent PRs claimed 491-493). Remediation options: (a) make the encoder conform to the nominal contract (truncation semantics for negative operands, explicit overflow modeling), or (b) revise SemanticProfileV1 to declare the coincidence-domain semantics explicitly — either way cert_writer semanticProfileId continuity and the modelprofile segment must move together in one coherent generation.
entries.resolution: RESOLVED (weakened — option b) 2026-10-07 on fix/semantic-profile-verified-semantics: SemanticProfileV1 declarations moved to the verified meaning; the Phase-2 encoder-conformance direction (option a: make the encoder truncate for negative operands and model checked-overflow reachability) is WITHDRAWN as the contract direction. divisionMode now spDivCoincidentNonnegative (Nim div (trunc) == Lean / (floor) on the nonnegative domain; no claim for negative operands) and overflowMode now spOverflowObligationDischarged (reachability not modeled; discharged via no-overflow obligations; checked/wrap coincide in the verified domain); spDivTruncTowardZero and spOverflowBounded remain as nominal V2+ encoder-conformance targets only. GlobalSemanticProfileV1 and SemanticProfileV1Hash regenerated in this single coherent generation (af30124e618db1dae9bc8ba95991f620f07077847a29d3f42b4fcd67b48bdf4d → d2c44f569ef61e349a915582c4237b1b747df4d30a4701712178655bdd5bc44e) together with the modelprofile identity segment consumers (identity.nim, canonical_verification.nim D2, attestation_orchestrator pinnedToolchainIdentity, cert_writer semanticProfileId fallback), docs/spec/semantic_profile_verified_semantics.md (new machine-semantics note), base36_sizing_binding_contract.md §4.1, data/certification/evidence-draft.json, and this close. Machine semantics measured: -7 div 5 = -1 (Nim trunc) vs -2 (Lean floor); -7 mod 5 = -2 (Nim) vs 3 (Lean Int.emod) — negative-domain divergence confirmed on pinned Nim 2.2.10.
entries.resolutionNote: Direction reversal justification: docs/spec/productization_contract.md and config/readiness_policy.json contain NO truncation/overflow guarantee (measured 2026-10-07, grep zero matches), so weakening the nominal declarations does not reduce any documented product contract — it removes an untracked nominal-vs-verified gap (the opposite of theater; the identity now names exactly what is proven). Behavior invariance: the declaration change is engine-neutral; the single behavioral consumer of GlobalSemanticProfileV1 (src/verification/batch_uap/ir_pipeline_runner.nim:1022) was aligned to overflowMode in {spOverflowBounded, spOverflowObligationDischarged} so SMT emission is byte-identical to the pre-weakening pipeline (includeOverflowDefines stayed true); GlobalSemanticProfileV1 has no other consumers (measured by search over src/, tests/, tools/). Fixture handling: the unsigned B-pinned draft data/certification/evidence-draft.json was regenerated to the new hash in this generation; the Ed25519-sealed artifacts src/verification/certificates/c14243cd….json and data/readiness/golden/negative/93af4444….json are NOT rewritten (no local minting authority; reissueReference only reclassifies status), per base36_sizing_binding_contract.md §9 their stored old-hash semanticProfileId fails closed against the new identity and re-executes — intended epoch semantics. Tests: test_attestation/test_project_setup/test_scope_identity/test_wpj4_ladder reference the SemanticProfileV1Hash constant and auto-adapt; test_overflow_conformance.nim smoke message updated; debt_engine --codegen + --validate run clean. Evidence: docs/spec/semantic_profile_verified_semantics.md.

entries.title: Coverage ratchet baseline downgrade was granted by two ambient env vars alone — the 'audited downgrade protocol' guaranteed nothing
entries.description: coverage_ratchet_gate.nim granted FAIL→PASS and lowered data/reliability_score.json from AXIOM_RATCHET_DOWNGRADE=1 + AXIOM_RATCHET_REASON (any non-empty string) alone; adminSignature was set to the attacker-supplied reason string. The .axiom/bypass_audit.jsonl append was best-effort (warn-only on failure) and the file is untracked — git history showed 4 downgrades with 0 audit entries. A missing/corrupt baseline defaulted to 0.0% (pass), and auto-bump rewrote the baseline with no record chain. Closure: request/authority separation — env flags are a request only; the sole authority to lower the baseline is a pinned-key Ed25519 signature (src/core/trusted/ratchet_authority.nim, keyid e6ccd0895af2b964, private half held offline) over the ratchet-specific payload '{tree_hash}|{old_baseline}|{new_baseline}|{reason}|{expires_at}|{jti}' (break-glass bypass_verify contract untouched); expiry bound, jti single-use (burned by granted AND refused records), payload binds tree+both baselines so retargeting/self-keypair forgery verify to refusal. Canonical audit is in-band: downgrade_history records signature+keyid+payload+hash chain (prev_record_hash/record_hash) for granted and refused outcomes; the local .axiom append is a mirror and a failed append now REFUSES the downgrade. Missing/corrupt baseline is FAIL (no 0.0 default); history is verified at load (granted records crypto-verified, refusal records evidence-only) and the live baseline must equal the last recorded state change once the audited regime has any record; auto-bump is recorded in-band as kind=auto_bump risk=none.

D4 expired approval → refused approval_expired. D5 fresh valid signature replaying a burned jti → refused jti_reuse. D7 the only grant path: pinned-key signature → exit 0, baseline 28.5→10.0, granted in-band record (payload+signature+keyid+chain head) + .axiom mirror entry. entries.title: void/try-discard bodies materialize as fabricated irLit(0) with retType=irtBitVec64 — latent void-semantics distortion, unreachable through current kernel inputs, contained by loss flags + census classification
entries.description: The IR has no void type (grep irtVoid over axiom_ir.nim: zero matches) and the statement-level translator drops nnkDiscardStmt/ckDiscardStmt, so void-shaped function bodies are silently fabricated rather than refused. Measured mechanism (reproduction 2026-10-08, worktree chore/void-discard-investigation, probes tmp/void_discard_repro.nim + tmp/void_discard_materializer_repro.nim, both gitignored): (1) macro registry path — ast_to_ir.nim convertBodyFrom drops nnkDiscardStmt (:716-717) and falls back to irLit(0) when no trailing value expression exists (:969-970); convertFuncDef defaults a void return (nnkEmpty formalParams[0]) to irTypeBitVec64() (:1367-1370); axiomImpl (axiom_pragmas_macros.nim:674-712) registers the result with hardcoded effectKind=Pure and isKern=true without the hasUnsupportedPatterns guard axiomTryImpl applies (:753-761). Repro: proc vdVoidIf(n: int) {axiomImpl} = if n > 0: discard registered as ret=irtBitVec64 body=If(Bin(boGt),Lit(0),Lit(0)); discard-only body registered as Lit(0). ir_inline_pass.inlineSmallFunctions then mechanically inlines any caller irCall to such a callee (repro: caller Let(u,Call(vdVoidIf),Lit(7)) -> Let(u,Let(__inl_2,n,If(boGt,Lit(0),Lit(0))),Lit(7))) — the pass itself is correct, the fabrication is upstream. (2) external materializer path (pnodeToCanon/axiomBodyCanon) — ckDiscardStmt dropped (ast_to_ir.nim:1255-1256), whole try/except-discard statements dropped to Lit(0) losing real assignments (repro: subjectTry 'try: result = 3 except: discard' materialized as body=Lit(0), translationLossFree=false), and void call statements are dropped from caller bodies BEFORE ir_inline_pass ever sees them (repro: subjectCaller 'helperVoid(x); x+1' materialized as Bin(boAdd); inline pass over env=[caller, helperVoid] is a no-op). ATTRIBUTION VERDICT (background task 2026-10-08): NOT an ir_inline_pass bug (it never introduces or mangles void/discard), NOT a Nim language quirk (Context7 Nim official manual: discard is a null statement/explicit value-ignoring, void has no value — dropping discard statements is correct expression-IR translation; fabricating BitVec64(0) is Axiom's own IR value-domain limitation), and NOT verification-affecting today: (i) zero void-returning axiomImpl/axiomTryImpl functions exist under src/ (scan 2026-10-08) so the registry path never feeds a void callee to the inline pass; (ii) the materializer path drops void calls pre-inline; (iii) lossy materializations carry translationLossFree=false/bindingUniverseComplete=false (external_ir_materializer.nim:293-302) which fail-closes semantic facts (semantic_environment.nim:219-222 rejects ALL facts) and census eligibility (candidate_eligibility.nim buvLossyBindingRegion/buvLossyPropositionRegion -> censusEligible=false, crrSemanticUnresolvedFact), and composite claim carriers refuse loss-marked bodies (axiom_engine.nim:1558-1563). Registered per ADR-0029 §5 (debt projection writer authority — manual registry edit is the approved surface) following the DEBT#494 registration style; deliberately NOT patched in code (§0.12: a root fix requires adding a void/statement domain to the IR — an expressiveness extension, not a minimal change, for a mechanism with zero current reachability). Remediation options: (a) add an explicit void/absent-value IR type + fail-closed refusal in both convertBody paths for void bodies and dropped control-flow statements, or (b) make axiomImpl apply the same hasUnsupportedPatterns guard axiomTryImpl uses so void/try/discard-shaped kernel functions degrade to axiomOpaque instead of registering fabricated BitVec64 IR; either way the inline pass env assembly (ir_pipeline_runner.nim runIrPipelinesFor) should refuse env entries whose bodies contain fabricated-region markers. Follow-up trigger: any new axiomImpl/axiomTryImpl function with a void return, or any external-subject selection that admits lossy singles to BMC.

entries.title: S5 build-skip SUPPLY REUSE is unreachable in production: ci-cache-publisher single-flight lets the ircheck-less lane-path partial entry permanently evict the verified-complete base-path entry for every freshly landed tree
entries.description: J3 §3.1 / ADR-0032 S5 build-skip (PR #645, pin dc92faf8) guarantees compile skip when the restored B payload is a verified complete supply (4 binaries + ircheck + fingerprint + nimcache). Measured 2026-10-09 (acceptance doc docs/evidence/s5_build_skip_acceptance_2026-10-09.md, run 37911842509) and re-measured 2026-10-10 with three independent reproductions (runs 38022092775 / 38022242393 / 38023152483 — attest/build-base-artifacts walls 3m54s / 3m47s / 4m13s, each logging 'AXIOM_CACHE_B_VERIFY: RESULT OK — 4/4' (partial entry restored as a normal HIT), '[s5] verified supply absent: proofs/.lake/build/bin/ircheck' and 'S5 COLD BUILD'). The leak is structural, four legs: (1) lane production gap — runner-pool-acceptance.yml ci-bootstrap runs only `make ci-compile -j4` (the Lake smoke runs in a mktemp scratch dir), so the lane artifact's proofs/.lake structurally lacks ircheck; (2) lane verification gap — the publisher's lane fingerprint manifest files map lists only 4 files, so consumer b-verify passes the ircheck-less partial entry as 'RESULT OK — 4/4' (the base fingerprint already carried ircheck — the asymmetry is the fingerprint's); (3) single-flight permanent preemption — the publisher saves the lane (partial) entry first and the base (verified-complete) entry second; when both target the same key (every fresh landing where B == the freshly landed tree), the base save is withheld ('base key exists — save withheld (single-flight)') and because GitHub cache keys are immutable the partial entry preempts the key forever; (4) consumer gap — setup-axiom-toolchain b-verify never required ircheck in the files map and B_PROBE probes only the 4 Nim binaries, so the missing fifth supply member was invisible end-to-end. The S5 skip path is fail-closed correct and the job2 judgment is invariant, but the HIT guarantee could not fire for any tree that ever had a lane-path save first. Registered per §0.9 (the v2 registration on PR #652's branch; this entry is the canonical main registration).

entries.resolutionNote: FIXED 2026-10-10 on fix/s5-ircheck-supply (VS-1 slice) — all four legs closed in one coherent generation. Because GitHub cache keys are immutable, 'replace the partial entry at the same key' is impossible on the platform, so the base-verified-complete priority rule (partial→complete promotion, partial entries never treated as a normal HIT) is realized as three honest mechanisms: (a) complete-by-construction writers — the publisher's lane verify loop, lane fingerprint manifest and the lane artifact manifest are extended to the full 5-file set (ircheck included) with fail-closed sha256/test -x, so an incomplete payload can no longer be saved under ANY key, and runner-pool-acceptance.yml ci-bootstrap now produces ircheck via the canonical `cd proofs && lake build ircheck` (mirroring admission-check [build]); (b) consumer completeness gate — setup-axiom-toolchain b-verify enforces the required 5-file manifest set, so a restored partial entry (legacy generation) is DISCARDED instead of reused, making 'RESULT OK — 5/5' the structural complete-payload marker, and B_PROBE asserts ircheck presence+exec (a Lean binary carries no Nim BuildSourceHash, so --check-provenance is undefined for it — its anchor is the b-verify files-map digest plus the presence/exec re-assertion; absence = FAIL → discard); (c) generation rotation — the action.yml script_hash change rotates a_fp, invalidating every preempted legacy key exactly once (the documented one-shot cold). Single-flight withholding remains and is now benign: it only ever withholds a duplicate save of an already-complete same-generation entry. Contract tests: tests/ci/test_b_cache_anchor.nim updated to the 5-file contract and extended — (h) pins 'RESULT OK — 5/5', new (r) incomplete-manifest discard, new (p5) ircheck-absent probe discard; 37/37 [OK]. Evidence: docs/evidence/s5_build_skip_acceptance_2026-10-09.md v3 (2026-10-10 COLD reproduction logs of the three runs above). Fulfills the DEBT#502 reservation recorded in DEBT#503's description (PR #652 registered the same finding on its branch; this entry is the canonical main registration carrying the fix). entries.description: Semantic authority split per DECISION-0630 (src/core/types/verification_tier.nim:104-106: re-interpretations of the certificate status truth table elsewhere are semantic authority splits and must be projected through the contract). The private func tierToCertStatusString (src/verification/proof_state_projection.nim:202-213) re-derives tier-to-certificate-status instead of consuming the canonical 1-arg mapping tierToCertStatus/tierToStatusString (src/core/types/certificate_types.nim:95-107), which cert_writer.nim:196-200 explicitly declares canonical ('Do NOT redefine them here'). The mirror's leading comment (:203) claims 'Mirrors cert_writer.tierToStatusString' — FALSE/stale: the mirror emits vtZ3Only→certZ3Verified and vtKInduction→certZ3Verified where the canonical maps certZ3Candidate (certificate_types.nim:99-100), vtUfAbstract→certLeanVerified where the canonical maps certZ3Candidate (:104), and vtNone→certRed where the canonical maps certNoObligation (:103); only vtDual→certGreen and vtLeanOnly→certLeanVerified agree. (b) certZ3Verified is the documented legacy spelling of certZ3Candidate (verification_tier.nim:148-149), so the vtZ3Only/vtKInduction arms are lower-bound-consistent but non-canonical; the vtUfAbstract→certLeanVerified arm has no such cover (certLeanVerified ⟹ leanVerified, verification_tier.nim:150 and :161-162). entries.title: A-layer toolchain cache stores/restores an incomplete toolchain, and missing nimble packages are silently absorbed as empty --path: flags
entries.description: Measured 2026-10-27 while diagnosing PR #1110 required checks. Surface: runs 40463425766 / 40463425798 failed with `src/cli/install_ax_cas.nim(23, 17) Error: cannot open file: checksums/sha2`. The effective compile line carried TWO empty path arguments: `... --path:tools --path: --path:`. (a) ci/checker.mk:16-17 and Makefile:15-16 define `CHECKSUMS_PATH := $(wildcard $(NIMBLE_PKGS)/checksums-*)` / `FUSION_PATH := $(wildcard ...fusion-*)`. When the package is absent the wildcard expands to the EMPTY STRING and is interpolated verbatim into NIM_TOOL_FLAGS as `--path:$(CHECKSUMS_PATH)`. An empty path argument is not a compile error but a no-op, so a missing dependency cannot fail closed at the argument layer. (b) config.nims:337-339 disables the nimble fallback with `switch("noNimblePath")` and then re-enables it only `when withDir(thisDir(), system.fileExists("nimble.paths"))` — when nimble.paths is absent the guard silently does nothing. nimble.paths is gitignored and is NOT inside the A cache paths (~/.nimble, ~/.choosenim, ~/.elan, ~/.local/bin), so restoring the cache can never create it. The combination (nimble packages absent AND nimble.paths absent) therefore makes dependency resolution fail silently rather than loudly. Cache-content evidence: the single key axiom-a-Linux-8497f84b2b8334c4-... was observed at 1115 MB (2026-10-26) and at 847 MB (2026-10-27T06:28:40Z), i.e. the later publisher committed a PARTIAL install during a network-failure window. setup-axiom-toolchain's A-probe checks only nim/lean/z3 versions (`AXIOM_CACHE_A_VERIFY: OK — nim=2.2.10 lean=4.33.0 z3=4.13.3`) and never the nimble package set, while the same run skipped `Install project Nim dependencies` because its `if:` (cache-hit != true || a-verify-ok != true || a-probe-ok != true) was false. 'Verify OK' and 'dependencies not installed' therefore hold simultaneously. Per AGENTS.md §0.9 this is theater: it looks like it guarantees the toolchain and does not. Registered, not silently patched.

entries.title: rust lane claims exactly-one-match target resolution but execution re-binds by last-segment first document-order match — extraction/cert attribution can attach to a decl that is not the selected symbol
entries.description: Measured 2026-11-01 on the current build (re-confirmation of a 2026-10-12 read-only observation). Surface: the rust lane's target-resolution discipline claims exactly-one-match selection — `--target` matches candidates by full fun_decl name OR last segment and refuses 0 matches (NotFound) and >1 matches (Ambiguous): 'The rust lane requires exactly one match' (src/cli/rust_lane_cli.nim:500-517) — but that guarantee is not enforced at execution: the run loop narrows every resolved candidate back to its last segment (src/cli/rust_lane_cli.nim:545-547; lastSegmentOf :386-389), and the extraction primitive binds the FIRST document-order fun_decl whose last name segment equals that string (llbcFunctionToCanonical, src/verification/llbc_to_canonical.nim:1090-1127; first-match loop :1119-1126). In a Charon LLBC document where two modules declare functions sharing a last segment, 'exactly one match' degrades to 'the first document-order decl' — the Ambiguous guard's resolution is discarded before it can protect anything (AGENTS.md §0.9 unenforced claim). MEASURED (extraction layer only): a real cargo crate with m1/m2 both declaring add_u8, produced with the pin-exact Charon 0.1.281 (798016509139eb51f0d764645f76d068d34ba5f6) (src/verification/extraction_provenance.nim:68,73) via the lane's own producer call shape; the committed test binary bin/test_llbc_to_canonical_032157623CBD1A97BA40CCFA85BF015D83E8BBCF over the runB document reports llbcFunctionNames = @["add_u8", "add_u8"] and answers the add_u8 query with modulePath=axiom_rust_probe::m1, sourceIdentity=src/m1.rs:1:0-3:1 — always the m1 decl, in both polarities (runA: unsafe m1 first, safe m2 second → rceUnsupportedGrammar 'unknown' fail-closed served for the safe candidate; runB: safe m1 first → successful extraction, identical m1 identity served for either candidate). OBSERVED vs POTENTIAL (strict separation): ONLY the extraction-layer misbinding is measured. The certificate-issuance chain was NOT executed — no vault/ledger mutation occurred. The terminal identity-proof mismatch — certificate identified by the selector's scope-lock module path + lastSeg funcName (src/cli/rust_lane_cli.nim:618-624, :639-649) feeding writeCertificateFromUapResult (src/verification/rust_rust_pipeline.nim:991-998) while the proven body is the first decl's — is a structural code-path possibility, NOT an observed certificate; in today's measured state the misbound entry lands in the 'unknown' fail-closed bucket and provenance fails closed without GITHUB_TOKEN (src/cli/rust_lane_cli.nim:530-533). signatureHash is format-validated (64-char hex) but never compared to the extraction output (src/core/trusted/axiom_pragmas_procs.nim:167-168), so no downstream check would catch the mismatch today. Registered per AGENTS.md §0.9 (discovery is registered, never quietly patched); a fix is a binding-contract change (thread the resolved fullName into extraction and check the bound decl's identity against the selector) deliberately NOT made by this registration. Registry dedup: full sweep of all 240 entries (llbc|charon|first-match|last-segment|same-name|cross-module) — no covering entry; nearest hits DEBT-CI#003 (upload-artifact immutability), DEBT#442 (run-residue cert ambiguity pre-classification), DEBT#505 (replay-lane partition) are different layers. Repro: /tmp/axiom-dup-probe/{ctl,runA,runB} (crate sources + subject.llbc); probe-doc lineage tests/fixtures/rust/axiom_rust_probe/README.md:21-25, docs/spec/llbc_quirks.md:238.
entries.resolutionNote: FIXED 2026-11-02 (impl-method identity slice, work/impl-identity-2026-11-02 — the DEBT#510 closure proper). The fix replaces the first document-order last-segment match in llbcFunctionToCanonical with structured-name binding: the exact structured full name selects one decl; a bare last segment selects ONLY when exactly one fun_decl carries it; two or more is an explicit rceMalformed Ambiguous rejection that names every candidate's structured name (the reason embeds 'DEBT#510'). Inherent-impl methods became ADDRESSABLE: the measured Impl{Ty{kind:'InherentImplBlock', skip_binder:<type ref>}} name-path element resolves its owner through the dedicated item_names owner map (docs/spec/llbc_quirks.md Q11 — the general intern table conflates trait-space and layout ids, Q12) so the structured name is <owner nominal path>::<method>. The lane CLI (src/cli/rust_lane_cli.nim) deleted its local last-segment re-derivation and passes the selected candidate's structured full name verbatim into rustSubjectOutcome / rustGuardObligationAttempt / rustSubjectIssuance — execution binds exactly the selected decl. Contract: docs/spec/rust_certified_subset.md §2 'Target addressing update (2026-11-02)' (honest limits: trait impl blocks, scalar owners, and impl elements outside the measured penultimate position stay unaddressable; &self methods fail the monomorphic gate on their anonymous region generic before Ref decoding). Evidence: unit 21/21 (tests/unit/test_llbc_to_canonical.nim — m1/m2 add_u8 selections mutually DISTINCT, bare add_u8/speak/new → Ambiguous with both candidate names, exact Dog::speak selected-never-NotFound) and gateway 20/20 (tests/gateway/rust_lane_cli_acceptance_test.nim suite 7 — the real product CLI: bare targets → exit 3 Ambiguous naming both owner-qualified fullNames with no report document; exact structured names → one-target selection with the entry name being the full structured name; axiom_impl_probe::m1::add_u8 → the undeclared guard-attempt path, deterministic across runs), fixture tests/fixtures/rust/axiom_impl_probe/ (measured Charon 0.1.281 LLBC pinning both ambiguity pairs). Historical fields (description/files/lineRange/contentHash) record the pre-fix state.

entries.title: statusEnum in data/debt_schema.json and matchesStatus in the frozen debt_integrity_gate.nim disagree: the schema-canonical values in_progress and accepted are gate-REJECTED, and the gate-allowed value resolved is absent from the schema-canonical set
entries.description: Measured 2026-11-02 at origin/main ad8f67238 (read-only audit; registered per AGENTS.md §0.9 — discoveries are registered, never quietly patched — and §2.2: the root fix is blocked by FROZEN surfaces, so registration IS this task's resolution; this registration patches nothing). The debt status vocabulary has two disagreeing definitions. SSOT DOCUMENT: data/debt_schema.json:12-16 defines statusEnum = ["open", "closed", "accepted", "deferred", "in_progress"] described as 'Canonical lifecycle status. Prefer these values for new entries.' ACTUAL ENFORCEMENT: the frozen src/gate/runners/debt_integrity_gate.nim:60-62 accepts exactly ["open", "closed", "deferred", "resolved"] via matchesStatus; validateDebtRegistryImpl (:121-122) emits entry[N].status: invalid for any other value and the gate FAILs. DRIFT (both directions): schema-canonical in_progress and accepted are REJECTED by the gate; gate-allowed resolved is ABSENT from the schema-canonical set. data/debt_schema.json:176-180 additionally documents entry-level status as freeform ('prefer canonical values from statusEnum but freeform annotations are allowed') while presenting the enum as an adoption recommendation — the documented vocabulary and the enforced vocabulary do not close over each other: a contributor following the schema's own recommendation produces a gate failure. This is not hypothetical. MEASURED HARM: on 2026-11-02 the DEBT#511 registration used the schema-canonical value in_progress and the gate rejected it (entry status: invalid → FAIL); the workstream resolved it inside PR #1173 by re-registering with the non-canonical open and reverting debt_integrity_gate.nim byte-identically to the origin/main original (commit 2cd4977a0, 'fix(gate): FROZEN 서피스 순응 — debt_integrity_gate 원복 + DEBT#511 status open'), whose own commit message records 'push-admissibility check-repository-surface가 src/gate/**(FROZEN, policyVersion 91, BASE_SHA 바인딩) 아래 debt_integrity_gate.nim의 3줄 enum 정렬을 SURFACE_FORBIDDEN으로 거부'. The only gate-compliant status for an unresolved entry is therefore open — in_progress, which the schema itself recommends for that state, is unusable. ROOT-RESOLUTION BARRIER: both surfaces that would have to move are FROZEN — src/gate/** (search-TCB FROZEN glob) and config/repository_surface.json itself (policyVersion 91; classification is judged against the BASE policy, never the PR's own), so push-admissibility (check-push-admissibility-integrity → bin/surface_guard, reasonCode SURFACE_FORBIDDEN, tools/surface_guard.nim:258) mechanically blocks the alignment change; lifting requires architect-level authority (precedent: every v52-v91 FROZEN-to-CONTROLLED re-registration is human-architect-approved). contentHash is the sha256 of the matchesStatus canonical body (declaration :60 through final body line :62, trimmed — docs/spec/debt_registry_schema.md §6 rule 1) = the field value; the schema-side statusEnum block (data/debt_schema.json:12-16, exact line content — §6 non-procedure artifact rule) measures sha256:69e80b46fd97996b8b51ff132595f2a8404e0a8e180937cfa60e9294e29b14c2, recorded here because one contentHash field cannot bind both artifacts of the drift. STATUS CHOICE: status=open deliberately — the schema-canonical in_progress for an in-remediation entry is exactly the value the frozen gate rejects, which is the drift this entry registers (same compliance reasoning as DEBT#511's re-registration: 'the frozen debt_integrity_gate enum rejects in_progress, so open is the compliant canonical value'); resolution=UNRESOLVED per docs/spec/debt_registry_schema.md §5. Registry dedup: full sweep of all 242 entries (statusEnum|matchesStatus|in_progress|debt_schema.json|debt_integrity_gate) — no covering entry; nearest DEBT#268 (Architecture / SSOT; architecture_debt contentHash staleness) is a different artifact.

entries.title: validateLedgerSemantic's closed-record resolution check passed a literal true — the verdict was decided before the field was read
entries.description: Measured 2026-11-04 (registry-integrity-restoration). tools/debt_engine.nim validateLedgerSemantic emitted check(rec.id & " closed record has resolution", true, "resolution=" & $rec.resolution) for every closed BUDGET record — the condition argument was the literal `true`, so no ledger state could fail it: a closed record with a missing or empty resolution passed exactly like a valid one. The check was pure output theater over the parsed BudgetRecord enum, which cannot even represent 'missing' (parseLedger assigns rkFIXED/rkWONT_FIX or rejects the record). AGENTS.md §0.9: a check that cannot fail guarantees nothing; registered and fixed in the same workstream (never quietly patched).

entries.title: computeSourceHash ignores its path argument — buildGateRunners stores one identical global 5-file source hash for every runner, so the per-runner '✓ Up-to-date' freshness verdict is decided by files that are not the runner's source
entries.description: Measured 2026-11-08 (AxiomSourceHash removal investigation). config.nims computeSourceHash(path) never reads `path`: it always hashes the same fixed 5-file set (src/gate/runners/gate_hook.nim, src/gate/orchestrator_hook.nim, src/gate/gate_utils.nim, src/gate/git.nim, src/gate/types.nim) via one `gorge("sha256sum ...")` call (config.nims:114-138) and returns the 320-hex digest concatenation. buildGateRunners calls computeSourceHash(src) per runner (config.nims:173) and compares it to the per-bin stored hash in .axiom/cache/gate_hashes.json, printing '✓ Up-to-Date' on match. Consequences: (a) all 6 runners receive one identical stored value; (b) a change to conflict_marker_gate.nim, hotspot_coverage_gate.nim, structural_safety_gate.nim, hermetic_test_gate.nim, or drnim_gate.nim (none in the 5-file set) leaves the stored hash unchanged, so a stale binary is affirmed fresh — the per-runner freshness claim is unenforced. Operational exposure is currently nil: the manual nim task buildGateRunners has zero automatic callers (measured 2026-11-08: no ci/checker.mk, tools/build_all_gates.nim, Makefile, .githooks, .github/workflows, or buildGatesFromManifest path invokes it). The AxiomSourceHash runtime consumer of the same proc was removed as dead code in the same slice; this entry tracks the residual computeSourceHash uses, deliberately NOT fixed there (minimal-change discipline).
entries.resolution: computeSourceHash now hashes its path argument: slots are [path] + infra(path excluded, dedup, fixed order) in one sha256sum call; 4 runners produce distinct hashes; Python hashlib independently reproduced 4/4

entries.title: .axiom/cache/binary_checksums.json stores the global 5-file SOURCE hash for every line, not the checksum of the binary each line names — the filename and 'Binary checksums saved' echo claim binary checksums
entries.description: Measured 2026-11-08 (AxiomSourceHash removal investigation). The buildGateRunners checksum-storage block (config.nims:196-208) calls computeSourceHash(bin) and writes `<binName>\t<hash>` lines to .axiom/cache/binary_checksums.json, then echoes 'Binary checksums saved (atomic)'. computeSourceHash ignores its argument and returns the same 5-file source-hash concatenation for every input, so no line ever contains a hash of the binary it names — the artifact's name, per-line format, and echo assert a guarantee (binary checksum) that was never computed. docs/spec/gorge_inventory.md G1 still documents the ORIGINAL intent (`gorgeEx("sha256sum " & bin)` — 'SHA256 checksum of compiled gate runner binaries'), which the code diverged from when computeSourceHash was introduced. No code consumer of the artifact exists (measured 2026-11-08; the only binary_checksums references in src/ are the unrelated data/policy/z3_binary_checksums.json policy), so the mislabel is latent, not actively misjudged. Follow-up fix: hash the actual binaries (std/sha256 per gorge_inventory G1's own note) or rename the artifact to match its content.
entries.resolution: binary_checksums.json now records sha256sum of the actual bin/<name> content instead of the source hash; verified equal to sha256sum bin/<name>

entries.title: pre-push/pre-commit genDepend captures do not skip user cfg: machine-local ~/.config/nim/config.nims can shift hook closure identity
entries.description: Measured 2026-11-08 (VS-T dependency authority handoff). The hardened generator profile (tools/ci/generate_gate_closure_manifests.sh, flags from core/gate/closure_manifest.genDependProfile) pins --skipParentCfg --skipProjCfg --skipUserCfg --skipCfg for machine-independence, while the pre-push Part 4a/pre-commit Part 1 captures (.githooks/pre-push, .githooks/pre-commit pp_capture_manifest) omit --skipUserCfg — on a host with a user nim cfg their closure can differ from the machine-independent profile. Hook files are outside this slice's frozen set but the VS-T slice deliberately did not touch VS-1 hook logic (constraint: VS-1 stamp/hook logic preserved untouched).
entries.resolution: FIXED 2026-11-09 (workstream/precommit-usercfg): both halves closed. pre-push Part 4a: pp_canonical_flags appends --skipUserCfg (landed 2026-11-09, merge 8bb71bf). pre-commit Part 1: NCG_GENFLAGS now pins --skipUserCfg — the single composition point through which the same flag string flows to the genDepend capture call, the FLAGS: identity binding, and the stamp META line. Differential measurement (production pp_capture_manifest contract, temp HOME with pkgs2 mirroring the production nimble resolution): pre-fix, a user cfg breaks this capture outright (--threads:off → malebolgia 'Thread' undeclared; --define:windows → typedthreads 'pthread_join' undeclared; both leave no .deps → capture UNKNOWN → commit blocked), while --mm:orc is invariant (quirk 6c); post-fix, all four mutations (threads:off, define:windows, mm:orc, bogus switch) capture rc=0 with manifests byte-identical to the clean baseline (sha256 61cc6aadd23a6081…), and the cfg-free manifest is byte-identical pre/post fix (zero side effect). Global toolchain cfg ($nim/config/nim.cfg) is NOT skipped — the real build loads it and pc_identity binds its sha256 (TOOLCHAIN_CFG); nimble auto-discovery also stays on, mirroring the real build (measured evidence: docs/spec/nim_gendepend_quirks.md).
entries.resolutionNote: The FLAGS string change updates the pre-commit input identity by design: existing checkout-local stamps (vs1-gate-stamp/1, .cache/) mismatch on the next .nim-staging commit and fail closed with the canonical remedy (bin/build_all_gates --release), after which the mtime bootstrap re-binds identity+sha — the same one-time re-stamp PR #28 observed on first push. Hook profile mirrors the builder resolution otherwise: --skipParentCfg --skipProjCfg are already pinned, project cfg is expressed as repo-root-anchored --path flags, and -d:release mirrors the builder's release flag.
entries.bindingRationale: Hook edit would change VS-1 stamp semantics mid-slice (coherent-generation §2.5: one concern per cutover); trace: docs/spec/nim_gendepend_quirks.md quirk 6, docs/evidence/vst_dependency_authority_handoff_2026-11-08.md §10

entries.title: Closure-manifest pipeline cost: unconditional serial regeneration (54 gates, 64-92s per precompile run) and ~3.5s nim-binary sha256 per probe
entries.description: Measured 2026-11-08 (VS-T dependency authority handoff): manifest regeneration is unconditional before key computation (correctness-first: prevents undercount from undetected inconsistency) and serial by design (no parallelization in this slice) — 83.9s (run2, cold) / 92.0s (run3) / 67.2s / 64.5s (warm) for 54 gates. Toolchain identity validation hashes the ~9MB nim binary per loadProjectClosure call (~3.5s in non-release-compiled probe tools; no memoization by design). Full precompile wall: 78.9s (old baseline) vs 308-330s (cutover runs). All numbers recorded in evidence §8; optimization explicitly out of scope (constitution: performance data only).
entries.resolution: FIXED 2026-11-10 (workstream/closure-toolchain-hash, PR #59): both halves closed. Parallel-capture half landed 2026-11-09 (workstream/gendepend-lever; prior PARTIAL record: warm 54-gate regeneration 109.5s -> 11.5s, 54/54 manifests byte-identical vs the serial baseline, unconditional-regeneration and fail-closed semantics unchanged; docs/evidence/gendepend_parallel_capture_2026-11-09.md). Remaining half — per-call nim-binary sha256 in loadProjectClosure — closed by a process-lifetime toolchain identity digest cache (src/core/gate/closure_manifest.nim ToolchainIdentity threadvar): the digest is computed once per process, and the manifest NIM_SHA256/NIM_VERSION headers are still compared on EVERY read (per-read revalidation, verification_dag_contract.md §5); failed computations are never cached and a resolved-path change recomputes. The VS-T no-memoization rule governs closure/manifest RESULTS (gate_cas computeTransitiveSourceHash — untouched by this change); the invariance assumption (nim binary bytes unchanged within a process lifetime) is the same accepted pattern as gate_memo's process-lifetime `nim --version` threadvar caches, and no registry/spec document requires detecting mid-process nim replacement. Measured (docs/evidence/closure_toolchain_identity_cache_2026-11-10.md, main 5f3595a baseline): 54-call closure loop 186.3s -> 3.4s in debug tools (55x), 3.15s -> 0.12s in release (26x); warm precompile wall 14.6s -> 11.3s (-23%, interleaved x3 medians, same tree); transitive hash identical across the change and 54/54 regenerated manifests byte-identical (diff -r, both code versions); fail-closed fault injections preserved (manifest missing, forged NIM_SHA256 with primed cache, forged FLAGS, poison-direction forged-first). Incremental regeneration remains not pursued (by-design won't fix — it would require a staleness-key redesign against the VS-T unconditional-regeneration hard constraint).
entries.bindingRationale: Performance work is prohibited in this slice (correctness-first constraint); trace: docs/evidence/vst_dependency_authority_handoff_2026-11-08.md §8

entries.title: Closure-based CAS keys under-represent binary identity across worktrees: 4/54 gate binaries embed the checkout/worktree path in their bytes
entries.description: Machine-observed 2026-11-08 by the sibling VS-2.3 measurement agent on this repo: 4 of 54 gate binaries contain the checkout/worktree absolute path in their bytes (path-embedding compilation artifacts). Closure-based CAS keys hash source content only, so two worktrees of the same commit produce identical keys with non-identical binaries. Today's CAS is per-worktree (.axiom/cache inside each worktree) so no false reuse is possible; the hazard exists ONLY if cross-worktree CAS sharing is ever introduced. Registered as a structural constraint for any future cross-worktree CAS design (binary identity would need its own content-addressed layer or path-scrubbed builds).
entries.resolution: FIXED 2026-11-13 (VS-DEBT-1 registry reconciliation; D3 closure authority = approved 4-Slice plan): resolved-by-observation 2026-11-09 (workstream/ef-cas-isolation) — per-worktree physical CAS isolation is a machine-observed fact (same-commit two-checkout matrix: identical 54-key sets, 50/54 byte-identical, 4/54 differing digests as self-build proof, no cross-lookup) and the Owner adjudicated 2026-11-09 the fixed policy 'CAS sharing scope is limited to the current worktree interior', so the registered hazard (cross-worktree false reuse of path-embedding binaries) cannot occur under the fixed policy.
entries.bindingRationale: No current defect (per-worktree CAS unaffected) — constraint exists only for a future design; trace: docs/evidence/vst_dependency_authority_handoff_2026-11-08.md §10; deepened 2026-11-09 by VS-2b/3 build verdict (3-layer path-embedding mechanism §4, 4/54 quantification §8, landing re-verification §10): docs/evidence/vs2b3_build_verdict_2026-11-09.md; resolved-by-observation 2026-11-09 (workstream/ef-cas-isolation): per-worktree physical isolation is now a machine-observed fact (same-commit two-checkout matrix — identical 54-key sets, 50/54 byte-identical, 4/54 differing digests as self-build proof, no cross-lookup: B compiled 54/54 from MISS while A's cache was fully populated) and Owner adjudicated 2026-11-09 the policy "CAS sharing scope is limited to the current worktree interior" (final verdict — the earlier handoff/VS-2b3 'revisit before cross-worktree sharing' recommendation wording is now fixed policy, F parallelization rejected); reopen conditions recorded: (1) disambiguate identity of path-embedding binaries (binary-level mechanism refined: 2 plaintext NIM_STRLIT + 2 path-derived NTIv2 mangled-hash gates — §ffile-prefix-map cannot scrub either class), (2) define shared-cache write/read authority (single-writer trust boundary), (3) verify cache-key to artifact-identity match (stored-digest comparison — DEBT#524): docs/evidence/ef_cas_isolation_verdict_2026-11-09.md
entries.resolutionNote: Reopen conditions preserved in bindingRationale: (1) path-embedding binary identity disambiguation, (2) shared-cache write/read authority definition, (3) cache-key-to-artifact-identity verification (DEBT#524 — remains open). Evidence: docs/evidence/ef_cas_isolation_verdict_2026-11-09.md.

entries.title: CAS gate-binary reuse verdict is fileExists-based: post-store tampering of a cached binary is not detected
entries.description: Machine-observed 2026-11-09 (EF CAS isolation evidence, disposable same-commit worktree): with the lock current and the cache populated, appending 16 bytes to a path-free gate's .axiom/cache/gates/<casKey>/binary and re-running bin/precompile_gates reports 'All gate binaries up to date' + 'Nothing to compile' (rc=0) and reuses the tampered bytes verbatim (digest and mtime unchanged across the rerun) — the reuse verdict checks file existence only (gate_cas.nim:241-242 compileGateToCas, :180 resolveCasBinaryPathWithHash, :202 resolveCasBinaryPath; precompile_gates.nim:546-551 lock-path check); no stored digest is recorded or compared at HIT time (getBinaryHash is a lookup API, not a verdict input). By contrast, a MISSING binary is detected and rebuilt byte-identically (fail-closed). Separately recorded property: isolation (per-worktree cache scope, DEBT#523 observation) and integrity (post-store artifact verification) are distinct attributes — the tamper hazard exists ONLY if the cache directory is externally tampered with or a shared/multi-writer cache is introduced; in the current local single-writer trust boundary it is out of the threat model (not a requirement).
entries.resolution: UNRESOLVED — conditional registration; no current hazard (local single-writer trust boundary, per-worktree cache); revisit when cross-worktree/shared cache or cache integrity verification is required
entries.bindingRationale: Hazard is conditional on introducing shared/multi-writer caches or external tampering — both out of the current trust boundary; trace: docs/evidence/ef_cas_isolation_verdict_2026-11-09.md §4.2 (observed), §5 (code citations), §6 (key-scope contract and DEBT#523 reopen conditions this debt completes); reopen: introduce stored-digest comparison at HIT verdict when cross-worktree/shared cache lands or integrity verification is required

Check (j) claims a closed-world writer set per debt artifact, but the atomic --close path's materialization sites are absent from the discovered set: tools/debt_engine.nim writes data/debt_registry.json (line 2147), src/generated/debt_constants.nim (2150), docs/DEBT_REGISTRY.md (2151) and data/debt_ledger.json (2159) through atomicWriteJson (tools/debt_engine.nim:1825 — writeFile(tmpPath, content) + moveFile(tmpPath, path)), yet the probe shows collectWriteWrappers over tools/debt_engine.nim returns only idempotentWrite and the four call sites resolve to garbage targets (atomicWriteJsonRegistryPath,newRegistry and siblings) that match no artifact. Two links break. (1) Wrapper collection, resolver rule R3: atomicWriteJson's trailing persistence call moveFile(tmpPath, path) (tools/debt_engine.nim:1835) should bind the destination parameter path through rule R4, but splitCallArguments (tools/ci/proof_unit_consistency_gate.nim:1169-1197) drops the LAST argument of any call whose final argument is a bare identifier — the call's own closing parenthesis decrements depth to -1, so the depth==0 capture at :1189 fires only on an inner bracket close; destArgs is therefore [tmpPath] (length 1, failing the greater-than-1 guard at :1206) and sinkTargetArgument (:1199-1213) falls through to args[0], returning the SOURCE tmpPath, which matches no parameter of atomicWriteJson(path, content), so the wrapper is rejected. (2) The direct path does match the bare pattern token atomicWrite (RawPersistencePatterns, :184-186, no parenthesis) on those call lines, but sinkTargetArgument's no-parenthesis fallback (:1210-1211) returns the whole body, which resolvePathExpr flattens into a non-path string. Consequence: any persistence site shaped as a tmp+rename wrapper is invisible to check (j) — a false-negative coverage gap (fail-open for that shape) in the second-layer safety net; today the invisible sites are the canonical --close path's own legitimate writes, so no wrong verdict is currently produced (the registered owner entries are the legacy writeFile sites at tools/debt_engine.nim:2268/:2864 and the idempotentWrite projection sites at :265/:267). Nim os.moveFile(source, dest) argument order was verified against the Nim standard library documentation — the destination is the last argument — so rule R4 is semantically correct and the defect is purely the argument-splitting capture.
